title: The Thief and the Merchant
logline: A reformed thief turned cloth merchant is robbed by an impostor who dresses like him and fools the night watchman; he calmly follows the camel's trail to a storeroom by the port, takes back his four bales and the thief's cloak with them, then laughs and hands the cloak back when the thief asks for it.
moral: A cool head recovers what cunning stole, and a man who has put his own wrongs behind him can afford to be generous: he takes back what is his and nothing more.
tone: Light caper comedy: a quiet night heist played with masks on and masks off, a patient morning investigation, and a warm, funny ending between two men who understand each other.

beats.summary: A thief throws away his mask and becomes an honest cloth merchant.
He knows his goods: four bales, tied with his own tasselled knot (planted for the ending).
One night another thief comes to the market.
He dresses like the shop owner and carries keys.
He boldly asks the watchman himself to light him a candle.
With the watchman gone he opens the shop.
Caught inside, he plays the owner counting on his fingers; the watchman suspects nothing.
At dawn four big bales leave on a camel.
The thief tips the watchman two dirhams.
The real merchant gets a welcome he cannot explain.
Wax, scattered ledgers, and the four bales gone.
The watchman's story: a man and a camel.
The driver leads him to a storeroom by the port.
The four bales, still tied as he left them.
The thief's own cloak lies on top; the merchant takes it too.
The thief catches up and sees his trick has failed.
He asks for his cloak back.
The merchant laughs and returns it without a quarrel.

subtitles.ar: كان رجل قد ترك السرقة وتاب عنها،|وفتح دكانًا يبيع فيه الأقمشة في السوق.|عمل مدة في التجارة، وأصبح يعرف بضائعه جيدًا،|وكان يغلق المحل عند المساء ويعود إلى بيته مطمئنًا.
subtitles.en: A former thief repented|and became an honest cloth merchant.|He ran his shop for some time|and closed it each evening before going home.

subtitles.ar: في ليلة جاء لص آخر إلى السوق،|وقد ارتدى ثيابًا تشبه ثياب صاحب الدكان، وحمل مفاتيح معه.|رأى حارس السوق، وطلب منه أن يشعل له شمعة،|كأنه جاء ليتفقد حساباته.
subtitles.en: One night another thief came|dressed like the merchant, carrying keys.|He asked the market watchman to light a candle,|pretending to check his accounts.

subtitles.ar: بينما ابتعد الحارس لإحضار النار،|فتح المحتال الدكان ودخل إليه وأشعل شمعة أخرى.|وعندما عاد الحارس وجده جالسًا بين دفاتر الحساب،|يعد الأرقام بأصابعه، فلم يشك في أمره.
subtitles.en: While the watchman went to get a flame,|the impostor opened the shop.|The guard returned to find him bent over account books,|apparently calculating figures.

subtitles.ar: بقي المحتال في الدكان حتى الفجر،|ثم طلب من الحارس أن يحضر رجلًا مع جمل لنقل بعض الأقمشة.|حمل الرجل أربع رزم كبيرة،|وانصرف بها مع اللص، الذي أعطى الحارس درهمين.
subtitles.en: At dawn|the impostor asked for a camel-driver.|He loaded four large cloth bales,|departed with them, and tipped the watchman two dirhams.

subtitles.ar: وصل التاجر الحقيقي صباحًا،|فاستقبله الحارس بترحيب زائد بسبب الدرهمين اللذين ظن أنهما منه.|تعجب صاحب الدكان، ثم فتح الباب،|فرأى آثار الشموع والدفاتر على الأرض، واكتشف اختفاء الرزم الأربع.
subtitles.en: The real merchant arrived|to unusual friendliness from the guard, who thought he had been tipped.|Inside, the merchant noticed|candle wax and missing bales.

subtitles.ar: سأل التاجر الحارس عما حدث، فعرف خبر الرجل والجمل.|طلب إحضار سائق الجمل، وسأله أين نقل الرزم.|قاده السائق إلى مخزن قريب من الميناء، حيث وضع البضائع قبل شحنها.
subtitles.en: He questioned the watchman,|found the camel-driver and learned where the goods had gone.|The driver led him to a storeroom near the port.

subtitles.ar: دخل التاجر المخزن، فوجد الرزم الأربع مربوطة كما تركها،|وقد وضع اللص عباءته فوقها.|أخذ التاجر الأقمشة والعباءة،|وأعاد تحميل البضائع، ثم مضى مع سائق الجمل نحو السفينة.
subtitles.en: The merchant found his four bales still bound as before,|with the thief’s cloak thrown over them.|He recovered the goods|and took the cloak as well.

subtitles.ar: لحق اللص بالتاجر بعدما رأى أن حيلته فشلت،|وقال له إنه استعاد أقمشته كاملة،|وطلب أن يعيد له عباءته.|ضحك التاجر وأرجع العباءة دون مشاجرة، ثم انصرف كل واحد منهما في طريقه.
subtitles.en: The thief followed,|admitting that the merchant had recovered his goods|and asking for his cloak back.|The merchant laughed, returned it, and they parted.

new_assets.name: clothBale
new_assets.description: A tied bale of cloth, 150 x 105 at s 1, origin at bottom centre. Fields: col (cloth colour), dot, s, rot, sq, knot (true: bow knot and yellow tassel on top), tassel (swing angle), ghost (dashed outline only), tick (0..1 check mark).
new_assets.implementation: Rounded rect (r 22) filled with col plus Ben-Day dots (style dot helper), 5 px black brush outline. Each end: three curved fold lines 14 apart. Two rope bands at x -40 and +40 (brown #7a4a1e, 7 thick, black edges) and one lengthwise rope across the top. Knot: two loops (ellipses 18 x 10) and a 26 long yellow tassel (tapered triangle with 3 strokes) rotated by tassel; drive it with swing(t, tHit, 0.5). ghost: stroke only, dash [10, 8], alpha 0.5. On the camel draw two bales on the near side at the hump (offsets about (-45, -150) and (45, -150) from the camel origin at s 0.8, measure against mountSeat('camel', P)) and the tops of two more 30 units higher behind; make them follow the camel's kneel and bob by using the seat point.

new_assets.name: cloakProp
new_assets.description: A loose red cloak (#e2231a, dark red dots, yellow trim line) with states: draped (over a 300 wide stack: a sagging blanket shape 340 wide, 150 deep, 5 scallops on the hem, lift 0..1 raises one corner), held (hanging from one point: 90 wide at the top, 150 at the hem, 190 long, sways), flying (the same shape rotating along an arc), onHead (draped over a person's head and shoulders, 150 wide).
new_assets.implementation: One function cloakProp(ctx, x, y, {state, lift, sway, rot, s}). Each state is a closed polygon built from 8 to 12 points with a sine scalloped hem (amplitude 8), filled red with the dot helper clipped to it, black outline 5, a yellow line 8 inside the hem. Cross between states by swapping the drawing under a 2 frame squash. Worn state is not drawn here: use the person costume cape via pal.cape and pal.capeDot.

new_assets.name: harbourQuay
new_assets.description: Port quay strip, 1800 x 1230, ground y 900, for any harbour, sea voyage or dockside story. Left: ochre warehouse wall x 0..700, top y 360, with an arched double door x 300..520, top y 560 (opens 0..1 onto a dark interior), two barrels and a crate at x 80..240. Quay paving y 900..1230 with a stone edge. Right of x 760 the sea shows behind the quay edge from the horizon y 640 down to y 880. Bollards at x 1000 and 1500 with a slack rope. Dhow at x 1250..1650: hull 400 x 110 with deck at y 790, mast up to y 330, lateen sail with one red stripe, gangplank from (1180, 900) to (1270, 800).
new_assets.implementation: Bake the static parts once (bake): sky('day'), sea rect in blue with white dash rows, wall with townWall style blocks and dot shading, paving as in marketStreet. Live parts: townDoor for the double door (two leaves), sail as a triangle whose free corner moves with K.noise (6 units; 14 when filling at the end), wave dashes shifting x by t * 12 modulo their spacing, hull bob 3 units. Returns anchors {ground, door {x0, x1, top, cx}, bollards, ship {deck, plank}}. Take camX like the other strips. Gulls are Library bird {kind:'dove', fly:true} on a figure of eight path.

new_assets.implementation: As planned. Candle: stick 14 x 60 scaled by (1 - melt), flame teardrop with K.noise flicker, wax puddle ellipse growing with melt, light disc as a warm radial fill under a navy dark overlay (draw the overlay with the disc cut out, evenodd). iconBalloon: white rounded balloon with a tail, icons popped with overshoot.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English translation is a condensed summary and omits Arabic clauses (P1 knowing his goods and going home content; P3 lighting another candle and counting on his fingers; P6 where the goods were put before shipping; P7 reloading the goods and going on with the driver toward the ship; P8 each going his own way is shortened); both languages are kept verbatim as supplied.
The opening shows the man in thief stripes and mask for 3 s, throwing the mask away and turning into the merchant, to picture 'left thieving and repented'; default: keep.
The impostor wears the same blue robe and white turban as the merchant and is told apart by a reddish beard and a red cloak (the cloak of the ending); default: keep.
His change of clothes is played as a gag behind the closed stall (shirt and mask fly up, the turban rises), with a portrait of the merchant for comparison; default: keep.

Added business not in the script: the first key fails before the second opens the lock, the thief relocks the shop at dawn, and the merchant's bales carry his own tasselled knot (to show 'bound as he left them'); default: keep.
A thought cloud over the watchman (96.84) shows the real merchant giving him the two coins, his mistaken belief; default: keep.
The merchant wears the thief's cloak from 143.56 until he throws it back over the thief's head at 171.28, and gives him a knowing wink as one former thief to another; default: keep.

Invented lettering (18 items): EX THIEF, CLOTH SHOP, 4 BALES (twice), ANOTHER THIEF, SAME CLOTHES!, 1, 2, 3..., ALL IS WELL, 2 DIRHAMS, THE REAL MERCHANT, WELCOME!, 4 BALES GONE!, STOREROOM, MY KNOT!, THIEF'S CLOAK, ALL BACK, HA HA HA!, THE END, plus the card ONE NIGHT...; default: keep.
implementation_notes: Film length 179.98 s (duration 177.58 + end_hold 2.4): do not extend the hold; the limit is 180.0 s.

Take every cue from timing.json word starts (the times in this plan are those starts). Three words are interpolated in the timeline (عنها at 4.52, اللص at 141.30, أن at 158.62): do not hang a sharp accent on them.
Scale: people s 1.2..1.25 (about 300 tall, faces near y 640), camel s 0.8; ground y 900 everywhere. Keep faces and all key action above panel y 1250; the camera centre y stays between 620 and 780.

The two lookalikes: build one function manP(t, who) on person costume 'merchant' and pass pal only for the impostor (cape, capeDot, beard). The cloak is a costume cape while worn and cloakProp while loose; never show both at once. Ownership timeline: impostor 28.32..86.7 worn; draped on the bales 135.72..140.8; held 140.8..143.56; merchant worn 143.56..170.48; flying 170.48..171.28; on the impostor's head 171.28..171.9; impostor worn after.

Mask on / mask off for the impostor: polite face (lid 0.25, mouth 'smile', brow 0, tip -0.05) whenever the watchman can see him; sly face (brow -0.4, lid 0.4, grin) only when the watchman's back is turned or he is alone. Switch on the exact cue times given (46.5, 65.3).

Night light: draw the street or room, then a navy overlay (alpha 0.45 street, 0.85 dark shop) with the lantern and candle discs cut out of it (evenodd path), so light sources reveal the picture; then the eyes in the dark as two white dots above the overlay.

The four bales keep fixed colours and stacking order (red and blue below, yellow and green on top; the knot and tassel on the yellow one) in every scene so the audience recognises them in the storeroom.

Bale positions over time: shop alcove 0..67.6; beside the shop door 68.7..78.1; on the camel 79.2..(off screen); storeroom stack 132.6..145.0; on the camel 148.2 to the end. Shop alcove shows ghost outlines 107.62..111.0.
Set LIFE.t = t every frame so everyone blinks; give explicit lids where the plan names them. Listeners always look at the speaker (lookAt); the camel has its own gaze target in every scene.
Walks use walk() on a position function with footfalls for dust; the camel uses GAIT.camel * 0.8. No sliding feet in the time lapse: use held poses that cut every 0.6 s.

Sound: only six quiet effects, all in gaps (4.35, 9.2, 21.7, 86.95, 91.0, 110.7) plus the end chime at 177.9 after the last word; SND master 0.6. No effect for the coins' flight or the laugh: the narration runs over them.
Transition card ONE NIGHT... occupies the 1 s pause 21.4..22.4; switch sky, lamp and cast under its midpoint with paired camera keys 0.01 s apart.
Lettering never covers a face: labels go in the sky band (panel y 120..330) with arrows down to their subjects; counters sit above the load.
Use the panel-only shake from the template for the two door rattles and the bale landings (2 to 3 units).
warnings: Two men in the same costume can be confused on a phone: keep the red cloak and the reddish beard clearly visible on the impostor in P2..P4, and note that in P8 the impostor has no cloak while the merchant wears it; the label THE REAL MERCHANT at 88.9 resets the audience.
The 'guard' costume preset, storeroom, candle, ledger, keyRing, portraitMedallion and iconBalloon are planned assets that may not be in the Library yet; fallbacks are given in new_assets.
The narration has almost no pauses (five of 0.6 s or more), so effects are few by design.
The storeroom must stay readable when dark: keep the dark overlay at or under 0.7 and let the door light cone reach the bale stack by 135.7.
Camel loading: the Library load field stacks items on the hump; four 150 wide bales will not fit that way, so the scene draws them at the seat point (see clothBale).
S9 is 16.5 s with many beats (fetch, kneel, load, leave, tip): keep the camera wide during the loading so nothing is cropped.
